findings.description: W1 PLAN.md DAG/CRITICAL-PATH ARITHMETIC IS STALE BY EXACTLY THE SIX UNCREATED t41->* EDGES — docs/plan.md's phase_7 section (line ~772) claims 'DAG: 42 nodes / 76 edges' and 'cumulative critical path 28 edges'. Machine recompute of docs/state/dag.json TODAY: 42 nodes / 73 edges / 0 cycles / 0 duplicates / 0 self-loops / 0 dangling endpoints, and dag.json's own stored critical_path is a 30-node = 29-EDGE chain (t0,t1,t4,t5,t6,t7,t8,t11,t13,t14,t16,t17,t20,t21,t22,t23,t24,t26,t27,t28,t29,t31,t32,t34,t35,t36,t37,t38,t40,t41). Arithmetic proves nothing is missing from the DAG: phase_6 review measured 36 nodes / 60 edges; phase_7 adds 6 nodes and 13 edges (12 intra-phase_7 + the t35->t36 entry leg) = 73. The 3-edge / 1-edge gaps are exactly the six t41->{t37,t38,t39,t40,t41} transitive edges the survey wrote its prose from but did not add to dag.json (adding them would change no ordering, no cycle status and no gate). Classification: warning, plan-text-only. Remedy: the orchestrator corrects plan.md's two counts to 73 edges / 29 edges (or annotates '29 recomputed; 76/28 assumed the six transitive edges'); definer may not edit plan.md at review_plan (read-only). Do NOT add the transitive edges to dag.json — the 73-edge graph is the canonical minimal form that every prior milestone's review validated.

W2 t36 ac3's 'uv export >= 100 requirement lines' MEASUREMENT PREMISE IS WRONG UNDER THE NATURAL PIPELINE AND THE PINNED SUB-TARGET PRODUCES 53 — measured today in backend/: `uv export --no-hashes --frozen --format requirements-txt` emits 142 physical lines, of which only 53 are requirement lines (`^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+==`; the rest are the two header comment lines and indented '# via' provenance lines). So `... | grep -c '^[a-zA-Z0-9]'` = 53 (RED against a >= 100 floor) while `grep -c .` = 142 (green). t36 ac3's own text says 'producing >= 100 requirement lines', which is the countable interpretation. The gate is also semantically off: the sub-target t36 must pin for pip-audit is `uv export ... > backend/requirements-audit.txt` then `uvx pip-audit -r backend/requirements-audit.txt`, so the gate should validate the ARTIFACT the pipeline actually produces. Remedy (groom t36, pin ONE of, and align the slot label): (a) gate the export artifact's requirement-line count at a floor measured from the real artifact (`grep -cE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+==' /tmp/req.txt` >= 50, floor not exact per W10); or (b) keep >= 100 but define the metric as non-empty physical lines (`grep -c .`) and re-word the AC text at groom time is NOT allowed (AC text is builder-visible) — therefore (a) is the recommended fix: pin the metric that makes the stated 'requirement lines' phrase true and re-measure the floor. Fail-before: rc=1 at base (no uv export leg pinned / no Makefile target); pass-after: rc=0 with the parsed count echoed. Cross-reference: W7 records the same class (a premise number that a machine re-measurement contradicts).

W3 §17.8.2 TASKS 7.11 AND 7.13 ARE DELIVERABLE-MAPPED IN t41 BUT NOT REQUIREMENT-MAPPED — plan.md's phase_7 mapping table assigns '7.11/7.13 + §17.8.4 verification + REQ-PLAN-071' to t41, and t41 does own both deliverables (ops/diagnosis.md = task 7.11 in ac4; ops/deployment-health.md = task 7.13 in ac4; §17.8.4 verification = ac1/ac5). But machine grep shows t41 cites REQ-PLAN-071 (and REQ-PLAN-070 is cited by t36/t37/t38/t39/t40 only) and NEVER cites REQ-PLAN-070, so a forward coverage audit keyed on requirement ids cannot trace tasks 7.11/7.13 to t41 — the trace lives only in plan.md prose. This is the same citation-pin class phase_5 W2-W5 and phase_6 W1/W2 were filed for. Remedy (groom t41): add REQ-PLAN-070 (tasks 7.11 and 7.13) to t41's Metadata Requirements line and cite it in ac4's slot label and pinned command ('REQ-OPS-040..048, REQ-OPS-060/061/062, REQ-PLAN-070 tasks 7.11/7.13'). W4 t40 ac4's 'EVERY finding id' IS A SUPERSET OF THE Parsed-VOCABULARY ITS OWN UPSTREAM CARDS DEFINE — t40 ac4 requires a four-column register row 'for every finding id parsed from the five committed scan reports'. But the parsed vocabularies its ancestors define are narrower in two places: t38 ac2 parses only trivy VULNERABILITY ids ('every vulnerability id parsed from Results (when non-empty)'), so trivy MISCONFIGURATION findings (the recipe is `fs --scanners vuln,misconfig`) have no defined id vocabulary upstream; and t37/t38's conditional loops key on the ids parsed from the two .txt audits plus the JSON reports' own finding lists. If groom pins t40 ac4's id extractor more broadly than t37/t38's, the closed loop becomes unsatisfiable (a register can never be complete against a vocabulary nobody extracted); if pinned more narrowly, ac4's 'every' is vacuous for misconfig findings. Remedy (groom, in this order): (1) in t38's pinned ac2/ac4 commands define the trivy id extraction to cover BOTH Results[].Vulnerabilities[].VulnerabilityID and Results[].Misconfigurations[].ID (empty arrays yield zero ids, so the gate stays green today); (2) pin t40 ac4's extractor BYTE-IDENTICAL to the union of the t37/t38 extractors and echo the parsed per-tool counts on the gate's evidence line; (3) keep the counts-equality leg (register counts == parsed counts) as the machine arbiter, never prose. Verifier: reject a t40 ac4 command that parses a path no upstream card parses.

W5 STANDING WARN CARRIED FORWARD (not a phase_7 defect) — two structural conditions every phase_4+ review has passed under, recorded rather than fixed: (1) DEP CHAIN: cumulative critical path is 29 EDGES (recomputed; 28 as plan.md claims, 24 at phase_6) against limits.dep_chain_warn = 10 / dep_chain_halt = 20 (operator-owned config; docs/config.yaml is gitignored, docs/config.yaml.example is the readable copy). Both numbers are reported here per the phase_6 precedent. (2) DAG-vs-FRONTMATTER ARTIFACT: docs/issues/closed/t19.md is a context-stripped closure summary with no frontmatter, so its t19->t14 edge is dag-only; all 41 other cards (including all six phase_7 cards) match their DAG edges bidirectionally.
